No INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE call site exists anywhere in the TS app, and no migration ever seeds a row into this table (confirmed: db/migrations/1770880372830_consolidate_chart_of_accounts_fixed.sql creates the table but only seeds chart_of_accounts, never account_mappings). However billing/views.py's AccountMappingsViewSet IS live (router-registered at 'account-mappings', /api/billing/account-mappings/) and was a REAL, reachable vulnerability: queryset=AccountMappings.objects.all() + IsAuthenticated only, serializer fields='__all__' (organization_id fully client-writable), Django's model/migration (billing/migrations/0001_initial.py) only knows id/created_at/updated_at/organization_id (never learned the NOT NULL transaction_type/debit_account_code/credit_account_code columns — CREATE would 500, but LIST/RETRIEVE/UPDATE(organization_id only)/DELETE all worked unscoped for any authenticated user against any org's or the global CLC-standard rows). REMEDIATED this round: billing/isolation.py's new GlobalPlusTenantIsolationMixin — reads return global rows (organization_id IS NULL) UNION the caller's own org's rows (empty queryset with no verified org context, matching DirectTenantIsolationMixin's convention); creates always force the caller's own organization_id (a tenant can never author a global row); updates/deletes to a global row or another org's row are denied (PermissionDenied/NotFound); ownership class is immutable (organization_id is always re-forced to the caller's own org on update, discarding any client-supplied value) — there is no legitimate platform/system execution primitive in this Django app today to safely author global rows, so that path stays fail-closed rather than inferring platform authority from ordinary authentication. Classification uses a NEW narrow type (MIXED_GLOBAL_TENANT_RLS_REQUIRED, extended in types.ts this round) rather than being forced into GLOBAL_REFERENCE_DATA (which would falsely claim 'no tenant partitioning needed' when tenant-owned override rows are a real, schema-supported row class) or TENANT_RLS_REQUIRED (which assumes single-tenant-only rows). BLOCKED_EXTERNAL_ACCESS: the live-deployed Django Postgres execution principal (which role it connects as) was not independently queried this round; deployment wiring (.github/workflows/deploy-union-eyes.yml derives Django's PG* env vars from the same union-eyes-runtime-database-url secret Next.js uses) proves the INTENDED principal is union_eyes_runtime, not an empirically-attested live value. Evidence: billing/isolation.py's GlobalPlusTenantIsolationMixin; billing/tests_mixed_and_multiparty_isolation.py's GlobalPlusTenantIsolationMixinReadTests/WriteTests (11 tests: global-plus-own-org read scope, org-B exclusion, missing-context fail-closed, create forces own org, cannot mutate/delete global or other-org rows, update re-asserts own org discarding a forged payload); billing/tests_round33_restored_surfaces.py's wiring-lock test; db/__tests__/rls-storage-authority-django-reachability.test.ts's mixinSourceImplementsGlobalPlusTenantPolicy() (semantic proof the shared mixin source implements the null-OR-own-org filter and force-on-create, not just a name match) plus positive/negative fixtures and a real-route assertion. CORRECTED (2026-09-04, finance.ts round 33 correction — independent review rejected the initial privilege grant): the initial pass granted full SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE and TENANT_USER/TENANT_RUNTIME authority simply because a generic Django ModelViewSet technically exposes those HTTP methods once GlobalPlusTenantIsolationMixin scopes them — but this entry's OWN evidence already established there are no real TS write call sites, no seed path, the sole TS reader is effectively unused, and the Django model is stale (missing the NOT NULL transaction_type/debit_account_code/credit_account_code columns a real CREATE needs), so CREATE would fail against the live schema regardless. PROVEN (2026-09-04, finance.ts round 32, CORRECTED same round after independent review found a load-bearing lifecycle defect in the first pass — see the correction note at the end of this reason): closes the isolation gap round 31 correctly reopened this to NEEDS_REVIEW for. Django execution-principal facts (Phase 1/2; see apps/union-eyes/backend/billing/isolation.py's module docstring for the full evidence chain): per .github/workflows/deploy-union-eyes.yml's backend deploy step, Django's PGUSER/PGPASSWORD are DERIVED FROM the frontend container's `union-eyes-runtime-database-url`-backed DATABASE_URL secret — i.e. Django is INTENDED, by deployment wiring, to connect as the same `union_eyes_runtime` role (NOSUPERUSER/NOBYPASSRLS per scripts/provision-runtime-db-roles.ts) Next.js uses for its tenant-scoped client. BLOCKED_EXTERNAL_ACCESS: the actual live-deployed credential/role was NOT independently queried in this round (no read-only DB access available in this environment) — this is the intended principal proven from deployment wiring, not an empirically attested live value. This table has no Postgres RLS policy today regardless (only the 24 baseline-0108.ts tables do), so isolation is enforced entirely at the Django application layer. `BankAccountsViewSet` applies `DirectTenantIsolationMixin` (apps/union-eyes/backend/billing/isolation.py), which: (1) filters get_queryset() to `organization_id = request.organization_id`; (2) forces organization_id to the caller's own org on create, discarding any client-supplied value; (3) re-verifies the row's organization_id against the caller's before allowing update/delete, and forces it back on every update so a caller cannot reassign the row to another organization; (4) fails closed (empty queryset / rejected mutation) if request.organization_id is absent. CORRECTION (same round, independent review): request.organization_id was ORIGINALLY documented as set by auth_core.middleware.OrganizationIsolationMiddleware from the verified JWT organization claim. That was wrong in a load-bearing way — OrganizationIsolationMiddleware is Django middleware (config/settings.py MIDDLEWARE), which runs BEFORE the view, and therefore BEFORE DRF's authentication classes ever execute (DRF auth happens inside APIView.dispatch(), after the whole Django middleware chain has completed) — auth_core.authentication.OIDCAuthentication.authenticate() is the ONLY thing that ever set the request.org_id attribute the middleware read, so for every real bearer-token request the middleware always saw org_id as absent and request.organization_id was NEVER populated. All 20 of this round's ViewSets were therefore fail-closed for ALL real traffic (safe, but not functioning tenant-scoped endpoints) until this correction. FIXED by moving organization resolution into a new auth_core.authentication.resolve_organization_context() function, called directly from OIDCAuthentication.authenticate() immediately after the org claim is verified — the only point in the lifecycle guaranteed to run before any view/queryset code; OrganizationIsolationMiddleware now only sets safe defaults and no longer attempts resolution. Read+write isolation proof now spans two levels: (a) mixin-logic unit tests in apps/union-eyes/backend/billing/tests_isolation.py (mocked queryset/serializer, proves the filter/force/reject decisions), and (b) REAL request-lifecycle integration tests in apps/union-eyes/backend/billing/tests_request_lifecycle.py, which call the actual OIDCAuthentication.authenticate() (mocking only the JWKS network call and the Organizations DB query — no reachable Postgres/JWKS server in this sandbox) and then run the real mixin against the SAME request object authenticate() populated, never test-injecting request.organization_id directly — including a negative fixture proving the mixin alone, without this propagation, stays fail-closed rather than silently working. Run via `python -m unittest billing.tests_isolation billing.tests_request_lifecycle` (16 + 7 tests, all pass). Direct NOT NULL-in-practice organization_id column confirmed in billing/models.py.

This table has no Postgres RLS policy today regardless (only the 24 baseline-0108.ts tables do), so isolation is enforced entirely at the Django application layer. `FinancialPeriodsViewSet` applies `DirectTenantIsolationMixin` (apps/union-eyes/backend/billing/isolation.py), which: (1) filters get_queryset() to `organization_id = request.organization_id`; (2) forces organization_id to the caller's own org on create, discarding any client-supplied value; (3) re-verifies the row's organization_id against the caller's before allowing update/delete, and forces it back on every update so a caller cannot reassign the row to another organization; (4) fails closed (empty queryset / rejected mutation) if request.organization_id is absent. authority.reason: PROVEN (2026-09-04, finance.ts round 32, CORRECTED same round after independent review found a load-bearing lifecycle defect in the first pass — see the correction note at the end of this reason): closes the isolation gap round 31 correctly reopened this to NEEDS_REVIEW for. Django execution-principal facts (Phase 1/2; see apps/union-eyes/backend/billing/isolation.py's module docstring for the full evidence chain): per .github/workflows/deploy-union-eyes.yml's backend deploy step, Django's PGUSER/PGPASSWORD are DERIVED FROM the frontend container's `union-eyes-runtime-database-url`-backed DATABASE_URL secret — i.e. Django is INTENDED, by deployment wiring, to connect as the same `union_eyes_runtime` role (NOSUPERUSER/NOBYPASSRLS per scripts/provision-runtime-db-roles.ts) Next.js uses for its tenant-scoped client. BLOCKED_EXTERNAL_ACCESS: the actual live-deployed credential/role was NOT independently queried in this round (no read-only DB access available in this environment) — this is the intended principal proven from deployment wiring, not an empirically attested live value. This table has no Postgres RLS policy today regardless (only the 24 baseline-0108.ts tables do), so isolation is enforced entirely at the Django application layer. `PaymentCyclesViewSet` applies `DirectTenantIsolationMixin` (apps/union-eyes/backend/billing/isolation.py), which: (1) filters get_queryset() to `organization_id = request.organization_id`; (2) forces organization_id to the caller's own org on create, discarding any client-supplied value; (3) re-verifies the row's organization_id against the caller's before allowing update/delete, and forces it back on every update so a caller cannot reassign the row to another organization; (4) fails closed (empty queryset / rejected mutation) if request.organization_id is absent. CORRECTION (same round, independent review): request.organization_id was ORIGINALLY documented as set by auth_core.middleware.OrganizationIsolationMiddleware from the verified JWT organization claim. That was wrong in a load-bearing way — OrganizationIsolationMiddleware is Django middleware (config/settings.py MIDDLEWARE), which runs BEFORE the view, and therefore BEFORE DRF's authentication classes ever execute (DRF auth happens inside APIView.dispatch(), after the whole Django middleware chain has completed) — auth_core.authentication.OIDCAuthentication.authenticate() is the ONLY thing that ever set the request.org_id attribute the middleware read, so for every real bearer-token request the middleware always saw org_id as absent and request.organization_id was NEVER populated. All 20 of this round's ViewSets were therefore fail-closed for ALL real traffic (safe, but not functioning tenant-scoped endpoints) until this correction. FIXED by moving organization resolution into a new auth_core.authentication.resolve_organization_context() function, called directly from OIDCAuthentication.authenticate() immediately after the org claim is verified — the only point in the lifecycle guaranteed to run before any view/queryset code; OrganizationIsolationMiddleware now only sets safe defaults and no longer attempts resolution. Read+write isolation proof now spans two levels: (a) mixin-logic unit tests in apps/union-eyes/backend/billing/tests_isolation.py (mocked queryset/serializer, proves the filter/force/reject decisions), and (b) REAL request-lifecycle integration tests in apps/union-eyes/backend/billing/tests_request_lifecycle.py, which call the actual OIDCAuthentication.authenticate() (mocking only the JWKS network call and the Organizations DB query — no reachable Postgres/JWKS server in this sandbox) and then run the real mixin against the SAME request object authenticate() populated, never test-injecting request.organization_id directly — including a negative fixture proving the mixin alone, without this propagation, stays fail-closed rather than silently working. Run via `python -m unittest billing.tests_isolation billing.tests_request_lifecycle` (16 + 7 tests, all pass). Direct NOT NULL-in-practice organization_id column confirmed in billing/models.py.

Proved this empirically (not just by code inspection) via lib/services/rewards/__tests__/round36-cross-org-budget-boundary.test.ts and round36-award-issuance-atomicity.test.ts: a rogue Org-A envelope for Org B's program, deliberately given a NEWER createdAt than Org B's own envelope (so an ORDER BY createdAt DESC query would pick it first), is proven never read or mutated by any Org-B-scoped operation once the fix is applied. FIX: (1) createBudgetEnvelope now queries recognitionPrograms and throws unless program.orgId === data.orgId; (2) checkBudgetAvailability/applyBudgetUsage/applyBudgetUsageChecked/reserveBudget all gained a required orgId parameter with eq(rewardBudgetEnvelopes.orgId, orgId) added to every SELECT and UPDATE WHERE clause. TRANSACTION ATOMICITY (round 36): applyBudgetUsage/applyBudgetUsageChecked previously used the module-global db even when called from inside issueAward()/revokeAward()'s db.transaction(tx => ...) callback, so a failure after the ledger entry but before the award-state update would not roll back the budget mutation — the 'transactional operation' was not actually atomic. Both functions now accept tx as their first parameter (matching wallet-service.ts's applyLedgerEntry(tx, ...) convention already used for the ledger), and award-service.ts now passes its own tx and award.orgId through. Proved atomicity empirically: a budget-step failure (insufficient limit) leaves the award status untouched (never reaches 'issued'/'revoked') and only one ledger-entry call is ever made — the sequence is now safe for the real db.transaction() to roll back as one unit. DJANGO SIDE: RewardBudgetEnvelopesViewSet is genuinely reachable (config/urls.py includes unions.urls at 'api/unions/', router-registered at 'reward-budget-envelopes') but the Django model maps ONLY a nullable org_id (confirmed via _meta.get_fields()) — missing program_id and every financial field (name/scope_type/period/amount_limit/amount_used/starts_at/ends_at). No real TS or Django consumer of the REST endpoint was found anywhere (git-grep confirmed). Contained with a new local DenyAllPermission (backend/unions/views.py) — same 'no legitimate Django consumer' precedent as ai_budgets (round 35) and donation_receipts (round 33). RLS INFRASTRUCTURE NOTE (found, not remediated this round — out of round-36 scope): db/migrations/0097_nzilaos_rls_org_isolation.sql already runs a legitimate, working create_org_rls_policy('reward_budget_envelopes', 'org_id') (current_setting('app.current_org_id'), unlike ai_budgets' broken auth.user_id() reference) — but budget-service.ts's module-level `db` import never runs inside withRLSContext()/a system context, so app.current_org_id is never set for these queries and RLS's system_bypass policy (empty org context) silently applies, meaning TODAY's actual protection is entirely the application-level org_id filters this round added, not enforced Postgres RLS. PROVEN + REMEDIATED (2026-09-04, finance.ts round 36 — rewards financial authority): independently re-derived reachability and found a real, exploitable cross-org defect, then fixed it. TS SIDE IS ACTIVE: createBudgetEnvelope (INSERT, admin-gated via checkAdminRole()), listBudgetEnvelopes/getBudgetUsageSummary/getBudgetStatus/checkBudgetWithReservations (SELECT, already org-scoped pre-round-36), and applyBudgetUsage/applyBudgetUsageChecked (UPDATE, called from award-service.ts's issueAward()/revokeAward() inside db.transaction()) are all real, reachable production code paths. No DELETE call site exists anywhere (git-grep confirmed). PROVEN VULNERABILITY (round 36): createBudgetEnvelope inserted programId (client-supplied, only UUID-validated) without proving the referenced recognition program belongs to the same orgId — the program_id FK only proves the program exists, not that its owner matches the envelope's org_id. Worse, checkBudgetAvailability/applyBudgetUsage/applyBudgetUsageChecked/reserveBudget queried/mutated envelopes by programId + scopeType + date range alone, with NO org_id predicate — so an Org-A-owned envelope referencing Org B's program (however it came to exist) could be read/mutated by Org B's own award issuance/revocation flow, entirely bypassing Org B's real budget limits. Proved this empirically (not just by code inspection) via lib/services/rewards/__tests__/round36-cross-org-budget-boundary.test.ts and round36-award-issuance-atomicity.test.ts: a rogue Org-A envelope for Org B's program, deliberately given a NEWER createdAt than Org B's own envelope (so an ORDER BY createdAt DESC query would pick it first), is proven never read or mutated by any Org-B-scoped operation once the fix is applied. FIX: (1) createBudgetEnvelope now queries recognitionPrograms and throws unless program.orgId === data.orgId; (2) checkBudgetAvailability/applyBudgetUsage/applyBudgetUsageChecked/reserveBudget all gained a required orgId parameter with eq(rewardBudgetEnvelopes.orgId, orgId) added to every SELECT and UPDATE WHERE clause. TRANSACTION ATOMICITY (round 36): applyBudgetUsage/applyBudgetUsageChecked previously used the module-global db even when called from inside issueAward()/revokeAward()'s db.transaction(tx => ...) callback, so a failure after the ledger entry but before the award-state update would not roll back the budget mutation — the 'transactional operation' was not actually atomic. Both functions now accept tx as their first parameter (matching wallet-service.ts's applyLedgerEntry(tx, ...) convention already used for the ledger), and award-service.ts now passes its own tx and award.orgId through. Proved atomicity empirically: a budget-step failure (insufficient limit) leaves the award status untouched (never reaches 'issued'/'revoked') and only one ledger-entry call is ever made — the sequence is now safe for the real db.transaction() to roll back as one unit. DJANGO SIDE: RewardBudgetEnvelopesViewSet is genuinely reachable (config/urls.py includes unions.urls at 'api/unions/', router-registered at 'reward-budget-envelopes') but the Django model maps ONLY a nullable org_id (confirmed via _meta.get_fields()) — missing program_id and every financial field (name/scope_type/period/amount_limit/amount_used/starts_at/ends_at). No real TS or Django consumer of the REST endpoint was found anywhere (git-grep confirmed). Contained with a new local DenyAllPermission (backend/unions/views.py) — same 'no legitimate Django consumer' precedent as ai_budgets (round 35) and donation_receipts (round 33). RLS INFRASTRUCTURE NOTE (found, not remediated this round — out of round-36 scope): db/migrations/0097_nzilaos_rls_org_isolation.sql already runs a legitimate, working create_org_rls_policy('reward_budget_envelopes', 'org_id') (current_setting('app.current_org_id'), unlike ai_budgets' broken auth.user_id() reference) — but budget-service.ts's module-level `db` import never runs inside withRLSContext()/a system context, so app.current_org_id is never set for these queries and RLS's system_bypass policy (empty org context) silently applies, meaning TODAY's actual protection is entirely the application-level org_id filters this round added, not enforced Postgres RLS. This is a legitimate future-hardening opportunity (wire budget-service.ts through withRLSContext), not remediated here to keep this round's diff bounded to the proven vulnerability and its regression tests.

PROVEN + REMEDIATED (2026-09-04, finance.ts round 36 — rewards financial authority): independently re-derived reachability and found a real, exploitable cross-org defect, then fixed it. TS SIDE IS ACTIVE: createBudgetEnvelope (INSERT, admin-gated via checkAdminRole()), listBudgetEnvelopes/getBudgetUsageSummary/getBudgetStatus/checkBudgetWithReservations (SELECT, already org-scoped pre-round-36), and applyBudgetUsage/applyBudgetUsageChecked (UPDATE, called from award-service.ts's issueAward()/revokeAward() inside db.transaction()) are all real, reachable production code paths. No DELETE call site exists anywhere (git-grep confirmed). PROVEN VULNERABILITY (round 36): createBudgetEnvelope inserted programId (client-supplied, only UUID-validated) without proving the referenced recognition program belongs to the same orgId — the program_id FK only proves the program exists, not that its owner matches the envelope's org_id. Worse, checkBudgetAvailability/applyBudgetUsage/applyBudgetUsageChecked/reserveBudget queried/mutated envelopes by programId + scopeType + date range alone, with NO org_id predicate — so an Org-A-owned envelope referencing Org B's program (however it came to exist) could be read/mutated by Org B's own award issuance/revocation flow, entirely bypassing Org B's real budget limits. canonicalAuthority.reason: PROVEN (2026-09-04, finance.ts round 32, CORRECTED same round after independent review found a load-bearing lifecycle defect in the first pass — see the correction note at the end of this reason): closes the isolation gap round 31 correctly reopened this to NEEDS_REVIEW for. Django execution-principal facts (Phase 1/2; see apps/union-eyes/backend/billing/isolation.py's module docstring for the full evidence chain): per .github/workflows/deploy-union-eyes.yml's backend deploy step, Django's PGUSER/PGPASSWORD are DERIVED FROM the frontend container's `union-eyes-runtime-database-url`-backed DATABASE_URL secret — i.e. Django is INTENDED, by deployment wiring, to connect as the same `union_eyes_runtime` role (NOSUPERUSER/NOBYPASSRLS per scripts/provision-runtime-db-roles.ts) Next.js uses for its tenant-scoped client. BLOCKED_EXTERNAL_ACCESS: the actual live-deployed credential/role was NOT independently queried in this round (no read-only DB access available in this environment) — this is the intended principal proven from deployment wiring, not an empirically attested live value. This table has no Postgres RLS policy today regardless (only the 24 baseline-0108.ts tables do), so isolation is enforced entirely at the Django application layer. `DuesTransactionsViewSet` applies `DirectTenantIsolationMixin` (apps/union-eyes/backend/billing/isolation.py), which: (1) filters get_queryset() to `organization_id = request.organization_id`; (2) forces organization_id to the caller's own org on create, discarding any client-supplied value; (3) re-verifies the row's organization_id against the caller's before allowing update/delete, and forces it back on every update so a caller cannot reassign the row to another organization; (4) fails closed (empty queryset / rejected mutation) if request.organization_id is absent. CORRECTION (same round, independent review): request.organization_id was ORIGINALLY documented as set by auth_core.middleware.OrganizationIsolationMiddleware from the verified JWT organization claim. That was wrong in a load-bearing way — OrganizationIsolationMiddleware is Django middleware (config/settings.py MIDDLEWARE), which runs BEFORE the view, and therefore BEFORE DRF's authentication classes ever execute (DRF auth happens inside APIView.dispatch(), after the whole Django middleware chain has completed) — auth_core.authentication.OIDCAuthentication.authenticate() is the ONLY thing that ever set the request.org_id attribute the middleware read, so for every real bearer-token request the middleware always saw org_id as absent and request.organization_id was NEVER populated. All 20 of this round's ViewSets were therefore fail-closed for ALL real traffic (safe, but not functioning tenant-scoped endpoints) until this correction. FIXED by moving organization resolution into a new auth_core.authentication.resolve_organization_context() function, called directly from OIDCAuthentication.authenticate() immediately after the org claim is verified — the only point in the lifecycle guaranteed to run before any view/queryset code; OrganizationIsolationMiddleware now only sets safe defaults and no longer attempts resolution. Read+write isolation proof now spans two levels: (a) mixin-logic unit tests in apps/union-eyes/backend/billing/tests_isolation.py (mocked queryset/serializer, proves the filter/force/reject decisions), and (b) REAL request-lifecycle integration tests in apps/union-eyes/backend/billing/tests_request_lifecycle.py, which call the actual OIDCAuthentication.authenticate() (mocking only the JWKS network call and the Organizations DB query — no reachable Postgres/JWKS server in this sandbox) and then run the real mixin against the SAME request object authenticate() populated, never test-injecting request.organization_id directly — including a negative fixture proving the mixin alone, without this propagation, stays fail-closed rather than silently working. Run via `python -m unittest billing.tests_isolation billing.tests_request_lifecycle` (16 + 7 tests, all pass). Direct NOT NULL-in-practice organization_id column confirmed in billing/models.py.

Router-registered at /api/audit-logs/ via backend/core/urls.py -> backend/core/views.py AuditLogsViewSet, a full ModelViewSet with queryset=AuditLogs.objects.all() + permission_classes=[IsAuthenticated] + filterset_fields=['organization_id','user_id'] — the unscoped objects.all()+IsAuthenticated cross-org pattern (any authenticated user of any org could list/retrieve/create/update/delete every org's audit rows). organization_id is nullable: NULL rows are platform/system audit events, which a strict direct-org policy correctly keeps invisible to every tenant (fail-closed). backend/core/tasks.py archives (UPDATE audit_logs) on a background schedule (system). 0011 adds direct-org RLS (runtime sees only current_org rows; union_eyes_system full access for the archival job and cross-org compliance reads) — DB-level closure of the ViewSet's missing scoping.

PROVEN (2026-09-04, finance.ts round 32, CORRECTED same round after independent review found a load-bearing lifecycle defect in the first pass — see the correction note at the end of this reason): closes the isolation gap round 31 correctly reopened this to NEEDS_REVIEW for. Django execution-principal facts (Phase 1/2; see apps/union-eyes/backend/billing/isolation.py's module docstring for the full evidence chain): per .github/workflows/deploy-union-eyes.yml's backend deploy step, Django's PGUSER/PGPASSWORD are DERIVED FROM the frontend container's `union-eyes-runtime-database-url`-backed DATABASE_URL secret — i.e. Django is INTENDED, by deployment wiring, to connect as the same `union_eyes_runtime` role (NOSUPERUSER/NOBYPASSRLS per scripts/provision-runtime-db-roles.ts) Next.js uses for its tenant-scoped client. BLOCKED_EXTERNAL_ACCESS: the actual live-deployed credential/role was NOT independently queried in this round (no read-only DB access available in this environment) — this is the intended principal proven from deployment wiring, not an empirically attested live value. This table has no Postgres RLS policy today regardless (only the 24 baseline-0108.ts tables do), so isolation is enforced entirely at the Django application layer. `DuesTransactionsViewSet` applies `DirectTenantIsolationMixin` (apps/union-eyes/backend/billing/isolation.py), which: (1) filters get_queryset() to `organization_id = request.organization_id`; (2) forces organization_id to the caller's own org on create, discarding any client-supplied value; (3) re-verifies the row's organization_id against the caller's before allowing update/delete, and forces it back on every update so a caller cannot reassign the row to another organization; (4) fails closed (empty queryset / rejected mutation) if request.organization_id is absent. CORRECTION (same round, independent review): request.organization_id was ORIGINALLY documented as set by auth_core.middleware.OrganizationIsolationMiddleware from the verified JWT organization claim. That was wrong in a load-bearing way — OrganizationIsolationMiddleware is Django middleware (config/settings.py MIDDLEWARE), which runs BEFORE the view, and therefore BEFORE DRF's authentication classes ever execute (DRF auth happens inside APIView.dispatch(), after the whole Django middleware chain has completed) — auth_core.authentication.OIDCAuthentication.authenticate() is the ONLY thing that ever set the request.org_id attribute the middleware read, so for every real bearer-token request the middleware always saw org_id as absent and request.organization_id was NEVER populated. All 20 of this round's ViewSets were therefore fail-closed for ALL real traffic (safe, but not functioning tenant-scoped endpoints) until this correction. FIXED by moving organization resolution into a new auth_core.authentication.resolve_organization_context() function, called directly from OIDCAuthentication.authenticate() immediately after the org claim is verified — the only point in the lifecycle guaranteed to run before any view/queryset code; OrganizationIsolationMiddleware now only sets safe defaults and no longer attempts resolution. Read+write isolation proof now spans two levels: (a) mixin-logic unit tests in apps/union-eyes/backend/billing/tests_isolation.py (mocked queryset/serializer, proves the filter/force/reject decisions), and (b) REAL request-lifecycle integration tests in apps/union-eyes/backend/billing/tests_request_lifecycle.py, which call the actual OIDCAuthentication.authenticate() (mocking only the JWKS network call and the Organizations DB query — no reachable Postgres/JWKS server in this sandbox) and then run the real mixin against the SAME request object authenticate() populated, never test-injecting request.organization_id directly — including a negative fixture proving the mixin alone, without this propagation, stays fail-closed rather than silently working. Run via `python -m unittest billing.tests_isolation billing.tests_request_lifecycle` (16 + 7 tests, all pass). Direct NOT NULL-in-practice organization_id column confirmed in billing/models.py.

canonicalAuthority.reason: PROVEN (2026-09-04, finance.ts round 32, CORRECTED same round after independent review found a load-bearing lifecycle defect in the first pass — see the correction note at the end of this reason): closes the isolation gap round 31 correctly reopened this to NEEDS_REVIEW for. Django execution-principal facts (Phase 1/2; see apps/union-eyes/backend/billing/isolation.py's module docstring for the full evidence chain): per .github/workflows/deploy-union-eyes.yml's backend deploy step, Django's PGUSER/PGPASSWORD are DERIVED FROM the frontend container's `union-eyes-runtime-database-url`-backed DATABASE_URL secret — i.e. Django is INTENDED, by deployment wiring, to connect as the same `union_eyes_runtime` role (NOSUPERUSER/NOBYPASSRLS per scripts/provision-runtime-db-roles.ts) Next.js uses for its tenant-scoped client. BLOCKED_EXTERNAL_ACCESS: the actual live-deployed credential/role was NOT independently queried in this round (no read-only DB access available in this environment) — this is the intended principal proven from deployment wiring, not an empirically attested live value. This table has no Postgres RLS policy today regardless (only the 24 baseline-0108.ts tables do), so isolation is enforced entirely at the Django application layer. `DuesTransactionsViewSet` applies `DirectTenantIsolationMixin` (apps/union-eyes/backend/billing/isolation.py), which: (1) filters get_queryset() to `organization_id = request.organization_id`; (2) forces organization_id to the caller's own org on create, discarding any client-supplied value; (3) re-verifies the row's organization_id against the caller's before allowing update/delete, and forces it back on every update so a caller cannot reassign the row to another organization; (4) fails closed (empty queryset / rejected mutation) if request.organization_id is absent. CORRECTION (same round, independent review): request.organization_id was ORIGINALLY documented as set by auth_core.middleware.OrganizationIsolationMiddleware from the verified JWT organization claim. That was wrong in a load-bearing way — OrganizationIsolationMiddleware is Django middleware (config/settings.py MIDDLEWARE), which runs BEFORE the view, and therefore BEFORE DRF's authentication classes ever execute (DRF auth happens inside APIView.dispatch(), after the whole Django middleware chain has completed) — auth_core.authentication.OIDCAuthentication.authenticate() is the ONLY thing that ever set the request.org_id attribute the middleware read, so for every real bearer-token request the middleware always saw org_id as absent and request.organization_id was NEVER populated. All 20 of this round's ViewSets were therefore fail-closed for ALL real traffic (safe, but not functioning tenant-scoped endpoints) until this correction. FIXED by moving organization resolution into a new auth_core.authentication.resolve_organization_context() function, called directly from OIDCAuthentication.authenticate() immediately after the org claim is verified — the only point in the lifecycle guaranteed to run before any view/queryset code; OrganizationIsolationMiddleware now only sets safe defaults and no longer attempts resolution. Read+write isolation proof now spans two levels: (a) mixin-logic unit tests in apps/union-eyes/backend/billing/tests_isolation.py (mocked queryset/serializer, proves the filter/force/reject decisions), and (b) REAL request-lifecycle integration tests in apps/union-eyes/backend/billing/tests_request_lifecycle.py, which call the actual OIDCAuthentication.authenticate() (mocking only the JWKS network call and the Organizations DB query — no reachable Postgres/JWKS server in this sandbox) and then run the real mixin against the SAME request object authenticate() populated, never test-injecting request.organization_id directly — including a negative fixture proving the mixin alone, without this propagation, stays fail-closed rather than silently working. Run via `python -m unittest billing.tests_isolation billing.tests_request_lifecycle` (16 + 7 tests, all pass). Direct NOT NULL-in-practice organization_id column confirmed in billing/models.py.

(2) POST create trusted body.sourceOrganizationId directly — any steward of ANY org could create a clause 'owned' by an arbitrary organization — fixed to always stamp the authenticated organizationId. (3) GET/PATCH/DELETE [id] had no ownership/sharing check at all — any steward could read, edit, or delete any other organization's clause — fixed: GET gated by canReadSharedClause (owner or a sharing-level match), PATCH/DELETE owner-only regardless of sharingLevel (broad reader visibility never implies write — verified via a pre-mutation SELECT+ownership-check, not just a WHERE-clause miss). (4) [id]/share GET+POST (the sharingLevel/sharedWithOrgIds configuration itself) had no check at all, letting ANY steward view or CHANGE any clause's sharing settings — fixed to owner-only for both GET and POST (sharing configuration is owner-internal, not shared clause content — sharedWithOrgIds is also now redacted from the [id] GET response for non-owner readers). (5) compare/route.ts read full clause text/tags and bumped comparisonCount for every requested id with zero check — fixed to silently exclude unauthorized ids (not an existence oracle) and only increment comparisonCount on the authorized subset. Django execution-principal facts (Phase 1/2; see apps/union-eyes/backend/billing/isolation.py's module docstring for the full evidence chain): per .github/workflows/deploy-union-eyes.yml's backend deploy step, Django's PGUSER/PGPASSWORD are DERIVED FROM the frontend container's `union-eyes-runtime-database-url`-backed DATABASE_URL secret — i.e. Django is INTENDED, by deployment wiring, to connect as the same `union_eyes_runtime` role (NOSUPERUSER/NOBYPASSRLS per scripts/provision-runtime-db-roles.ts) Next.js uses for its tenant-scoped client. BLOCKED_EXTERNAL_ACCESS: the actual live-deployed credential/role was NOT independently queried in this round (no read-only DB access available in this environment) — this is the intended principal proven from deployment wiring, not an empirically attested live value. This table has no Postgres RLS policy today regardless (only the 24 baseline-0108.ts tables do), so isolation is enforced entirely at the Django application layer. `PaymentPlansViewSet` applies `DirectTenantIsolationMixin` (apps/union-eyes/backend/billing/isolation.py), which: (1) filters get_queryset() to `organization_id = request.organization_id`; (2) forces organization_id to the caller's own org on create, discarding any client-supplied value; (3) re-verifies the row's organization_id against the caller's before allowing update/delete, and forces it back on every update so a caller cannot reassign the row to another organization; (4) fails closed (empty queryset / rejected mutation) if request.organization_id is absent. CORRECTION (same round, independent review): request.organization_id was ORIGINALLY documented as set by auth_core.middleware.OrganizationIsolationMiddleware from the verified JWT organization claim. That was wrong in a load-bearing way — OrganizationIsolationMiddleware is Django middleware (config/settings.py MIDDLEWARE), which runs BEFORE the view, and therefore BEFORE DRF's authentication classes ever execute (DRF auth happens inside APIView.dispatch(), after the whole Django middleware chain has completed) — auth_core.authentication.OIDCAuthentication.authenticate() is the ONLY thing that ever set the request.org_id attribute the middleware read, so for every real bearer-token request the middleware always saw org_id as absent and request.organization_id was NEVER populated. All 20 of this round's ViewSets were therefore fail-closed for ALL real traffic (safe, but not functioning tenant-scoped endpoints) until this correction. FIXED by moving organization resolution into a new auth_core.authentication.resolve_organization_context() function, called directly from OIDCAuthentication.authenticate() immediately after the org claim is verified — the only point in the lifecycle guaranteed to run before any view/queryset code; OrganizationIsolationMiddleware now only sets safe defaults and no longer attempts resolution. Read+write isolation proof now spans two levels: (a) mixin-logic unit tests in apps/union-eyes/backend/billing/tests_isolation.py (mocked queryset/serializer, proves the filter/force/reject decisions), and (b) REAL request-lifecycle integration tests in apps/union-eyes/backend/billing/tests_request_lifecycle.py, which call the actual OIDCAuthentication.authenticate() (mocking only the JWKS network call and the Organizations DB query — no reachable Postgres/JWKS server in this sandbox) and then run the real mixin against the SAME request object authenticate() populated, never test-injecting request.organization_id directly — including a negative fixture proving the mixin alone, without this propagation, stays fail-closed rather than silently working. Run via `python -m unittest billing.tests_isolation billing.tests_request_lifecycle` (16 + 7 tests, all pass). Direct NOT NULL-in-practice organization_id column confirmed in billing/models.py.

canonicalAuthority.reason: PROVEN (2026-09-04, finance.ts round 32, CORRECTED same round after independent review found a load-bearing lifecycle defect in the first pass — see the correction note at the end of this reason): closes the isolation gap round 31 correctly reopened this to NEEDS_REVIEW for. Django execution-principal facts (Phase 1/2; see apps/union-eyes/backend/billing/isolation.py's module docstring for the full evidence chain): per .github/workflows/deploy-union-eyes.yml's backend deploy step, Django's PGUSER/PGPASSWORD are DERIVED FROM the frontend container's `union-eyes-runtime-database-url`-backed DATABASE_URL secret — i.e. Django is INTENDED, by deployment wiring, to connect as the same `union_eyes_runtime` role (NOSUPERUSER/NOBYPASSRLS per scripts/provision-runtime-db-roles.ts) Next.js uses for its tenant-scoped client. BLOCKED_EXTERNAL_ACCESS: the actual live-deployed credential/role was NOT independently queried in this round (no read-only DB access available in this environment) — this is the intended principal proven from deployment wiring, not an empirically attested live value. This table has no Postgres RLS policy today regardless (only the 24 baseline-0108.ts tables do), so isolation is enforced entirely at the Django application layer. `EmployerRemittancesViewSet` applies `DirectTenantIsolationMixin` (apps/union-eyes/backend/billing/isolation.py), which: (1) filters get_queryset() to `organization_id = request.organization_id`; (2) forces organization_id to the caller's own org on create, discarding any client-supplied value; (3) re-verifies the row's organization_id against the caller's before allowing update/delete, and forces it back on every update so a caller cannot reassign the row to another organization; (4) fails closed (empty queryset / rejected mutation) if request.organization_id is absent. CORRECTION (same round, independent review): request.organization_id was ORIGINALLY documented as set by auth_core.middleware.OrganizationIsolationMiddleware from the verified JWT organization claim. That was wrong in a load-bearing way — OrganizationIsolationMiddleware is Django middleware (config/settings.py MIDDLEWARE), which runs BEFORE the view, and therefore BEFORE DRF's authentication classes ever execute (DRF auth happens inside APIView.dispatch(), after the whole Django middleware chain has completed) — auth_core.authentication.OIDCAuthentication.authenticate() is the ONLY thing that ever set the request.org_id attribute the middleware read, so for every real bearer-token request the middleware always saw org_id as absent and request.organization_id was NEVER populated. All 20 of this round's ViewSets were therefore fail-closed for ALL real traffic (safe, but not functioning tenant-scoped endpoints) until this correction. FIXED by moving organization resolution into a new auth_core.authentication.resolve_organization_context() function, called directly from OIDCAuthentication.authenticate() immediately after the org claim is verified — the only point in the lifecycle guaranteed to run before any view/queryset code; OrganizationIsolationMiddleware now only sets safe defaults and no longer attempts resolution. Read+write isolation proof now spans two levels: (a) mixin-logic unit tests in apps/union-eyes/backend/billing/tests_isolation.py (mocked queryset/serializer, proves the filter/force/reject decisions), and (b) REAL request-lifecycle integration tests in apps/union-eyes/backend/billing/tests_request_lifecycle.py, which call the actual OIDCAuthentication.authenticate() (mocking only the JWKS network call and the Organizations DB query — no reachable Postgres/JWKS server in this sandbox) and then run the real mixin against the SAME request object authenticate() populated, never test-injecting request.organization_id directly — including a negative fixture proving the mixin alone, without this propagation, stays fail-closed rather than silently working. Run via `python -m unittest billing.tests_isolation billing.tests_request_lifecycle` (16 + 7 tests, all pass). Direct NOT NULL-in-practice organization_id column confirmed in billing/models.py.

canonicalAuthority.reason: CLOSED round 57 (final voting-integrity resolution): no direct organization_id; scopes through votingSessions.organizationId (session_id FK, NOT NULL). Django unions.VotesViewSet already DenyAll-contained (round 56). BALLOT SECRECY: voterId is an anonymized HMAC derived from (memberId, sessionId) via lib/services/voting-service.ts's generateAnonymousVoterId() — the real voter identity is never stored directly when isAnonymous=true; voting_sessions.allowAnonymous governs the product-level policy. SECURITY DEFECTS FOUND AND FIXED THIS ROUND: (1) generateAnonymousVoterId() embedded Date.now() in the HMAC input, making voterId non-deterministic across calls — silently defeating the 'already voted' duplicate-vote check on EVERY vote (a member could vote unlimited times); fixed by deriving voterId deterministically from (memberId, sessionId) only. (2) A DB-level unique index votes_session_voter_unique on (session_id, voter_id) was added (db/schema/domains/governance/voting.ts) for defense-in-depth against a concurrent-request race that a SELECT-then-INSERT check alone cannot close. (3) app/api/governance/elections/sessions/[id]/vote/route.ts accepted a client-supplied voterId and NEVER checked voter_eligibility at all — a caller could impersonate/duplicate ballots by supplying an arbitrary voterId; fixed to delegate to the same castVote() (server-derived voterId + real eligibility check) used by the sibling route. VOTE LIFECYCLE: insert-only at the API surface — no PATCH/DELETE route exists for votes (immutable once cast, matching the append-only ballot model). Regression tests added (voting-service.test.ts, governance-elections-session-vote-idor-fix.route.test.ts).

canonicalAuthority.reason: Resolved 2026-09-02 (round 17): userId-keyed (no organizationId column — real-time strike/event location tracking consent is an individual opt-in under Quebec Law 25, not org data). The manifest's own scan evidence cited only service files, missing the real, live HTTP routes: app/api/location/consent/route.ts (POST grant / GET check / DELETE revoke, services/geofence-privacy-service.ts's GeofencePrivacyService). REAL BUG FOUND+FIXED this round: all 3 handlers took `userId` directly from the client (POST body / GET+DELETE query string) with no verification against the authenticated caller — any authenticated user could forge another user's consent grant, read another user's private opt-in status, or revoke another user's legitimately-needed safety consent. Fixed: userId is now always resolved server-side via getCurrentUser() (lib/api-auth-guard.ts), never accepted from the request; regression test app/api/__tests__/location-consent.route.test.ts. This table needs a dedicated user-scoped (not org-scoped) RLS policy design if DB-level enforcement is ever added; currently enforced only at the app layer. POLICY-EXPANSION PREREQUISITE (round 18, recorded now rather than rediscovered during migration generation): today the service queries this table through the ordinary `db` import with no transaction/session-variable scoping at all (no `withRLSContext`/`withSystemContext`, no `set_config`) — acceptable ONLY because the 87-table RLS policy-expansion migration remains blocked/unimplemented and this table has no policy to enforce yet. Once a USER_RLS policy is built for this table (e.g. `USING (user_id = current_setting('app.current_user_id'))`), GeofencePrivacyService's requestLocationConsent/hasValidConsent/revokeLocationConsent must be moved inside a transaction that calls `set_config('app.current_user_id', <caller's own id>, true)` BEFORE querying — the same shape as withRLSContext's org-scoped set_config, but keyed by user id instead of org id. Do not add this table to the migration until that transaction wiring exists; otherwise every self-service consent request would silently return zero rows once RLS is enabled.

PROVEN (2026-09-04, finance.ts round 32, CORRECTED same round after independent review found a load-bearing lifecycle defect in the first pass — see the correction note at the end of this reason): closes the isolation gap round 31 correctly reopened this to NEEDS_REVIEW for. Django execution-principal facts (Phase 1/2; see apps/union-eyes/backend/billing/isolation.py's module docstring for the full evidence chain): per .github/workflows/deploy-union-eyes.yml's backend deploy step, Django's PGUSER/PGPASSWORD are DERIVED FROM the frontend container's `union-eyes-runtime-database-url`-backed DATABASE_URL secret — i.e. Django is INTENDED, by deployment wiring, to connect as the same `union_eyes_runtime` role (NOSUPERUSER/NOBYPASSRLS per scripts/provision-runtime-db-roles.ts) Next.js uses for its tenant-scoped client. BLOCKED_EXTERNAL_ACCESS: the actual live-deployed credential/role was NOT independently queried in this round (no read-only DB access available in this environment) — this is the intended principal proven from deployment wiring, not an empirically attested live value. This table has no Postgres RLS policy today regardless (only the 24 baseline-0108.ts tables do), so isolation is enforced entirely at the Django application layer. `DuesTransactionsViewSet` applies `DirectTenantIsolationMixin` (apps/union-eyes/backend/billing/isolation.py), which: (1) filters get_queryset() to `organization_id = request.organization_id`; (2) forces organization_id to the caller's own org on create, discarding any client-supplied value; (3) re-verifies the row's organization_id against the caller's before allowing update/delete, and forces it back on every update so a caller cannot reassign the row to another organization; (4) fails closed (empty queryset / rejected mutation) if request.organization_id is absent. CORRECTION (same round, independent review): request.organization_id was ORIGINALLY documented as set by auth_core.middleware.OrganizationIsolationMiddleware from the verified JWT organization claim. That was wrong in a load-bearing way — OrganizationIsolationMiddleware is Django middleware (config/settings.py MIDDLEWARE), which runs BEFORE the view, and therefore BEFORE DRF's authentication classes ever execute (DRF auth happens inside APIView.dispatch(), after the whole Django middleware chain has completed) — auth_core.authentication.OIDCAuthentication.authenticate() is the ONLY thing that ever set the request.org_id attribute the middleware read, so for every real bearer-token request the middleware always saw org_id as absent and request.organization_id was NEVER populated. All 20 of this round's ViewSets were therefore fail-closed for ALL real traffic (safe, but not functioning tenant-scoped endpoints) until this correction. FIXED by moving organization resolution into a new auth_core.authentication.resolve_organization_context() function, called directly from OIDCAuthentication.authenticate() immediately after the org claim is verified — the only point in the lifecycle guaranteed to run before any view/queryset code; OrganizationIsolationMiddleware now only sets safe defaults and no longer attempts resolution. Read+write isolation proof now spans two levels: (a) mixin-logic unit tests in apps/union-eyes/backend/billing/tests_isolation.py (mocked queryset/serializer, proves the filter/force/reject decisions), and (b) REAL request-lifecycle integration tests in apps/union-eyes/backend/billing/tests_request_lifecycle.py, which call the actual OIDCAuthentication.authenticate() (mocking only the JWKS network call and the Organizations DB query — no reachable Postgres/JWKS server in this sandbox) and then run the real mixin against the SAME request object authenticate() populated, never test-injecting request.organization_id directly — including a negative fixture proving the mixin alone, without this propagation, stays fail-closed rather than silently working. Run via `python -m unittest billing.tests_isolation billing.tests_request_lifecycle` (16 + 7 tests, all pass). Direct NOT NULL-in-practice organization_id column confirmed in billing/models.py.

This is genuinely global, webhook-invoked replay-protection infrastructure shared by two real webhook consumers: app/api/integrations/shopify/webhooks/route.ts and app/api/payments/webhooks/paypal/route.ts, both via lib/services/rewards/webhook-service.ts's isWebhookProcessed()/recordWebhookProcessed(). AUTH ORDERING VERIFIED SAFE in both routes: raw body extracted -> HMAC/provider signature verified (verifyShopifySignature / PayPal's verify-webhook-signature API) -> only THEN is the payload JSON-parsed and the idempotency check run -> only THEN is the handler invoked. IDEMPOTENCY KEY = (provider, webhookId) with a DB-level UNIQUE constraint on webhook_id alone; webhookId is the provider's own globally-unique delivery/event identifier (Shopify's X-Shopify-Webhook-Id header; PayPal's event.id), not an app-generated or store-scoped value, so a provider+webhookId collision across different integrations is not a realistic replay vector — the unique constraint also provides defense in depth against any such collision (second insert would fail, not silently overwrite). getWebhookSecret(_orgId) is dead code (only its own def + test reference it) confirming there is no per-org Shopify store model — a single global SHOPIFY_WEBHOOK_SECRET env var is used, consistent with the table having no organization_id column.
